scope: Resolved grouping decisions only; not the complete family inventory or Item 8 acceptance

groups.name: YUNG's Better Mineshafts
groups.rationale: These are biome, material, decoration and support variants of the same specialized mineshaft network generator. All share BetterMineshaftStructure and BetterMineshaftGenerator. Their structure definitions differ only in biome constraints and BetterMineshaftConfiguration. Rooms, intersections, ore deposits, tunnels and entrance pieces are generated components, not additional families. This decision does not imply that arbitrary structures sharing a generic jigsaw codec belong to one family.

distinctions.minecraft:mineshaft: Separate vanilla generator, registered but suppressed by the frozen Better Mineshafts hook
distinctions.minecraft:mineshaft_mesa: Variant of the separate vanilla generator, registered but suppressed by the frozen Better Mineshafts hook

intended_hostility.value: Hostile rooms within an abandoned mining network
intended_hostility.basis: Derived from explicit hostile-entity spawner assignment in SideRoomDungeon and ZombieVillagerRoom, not from structure naming or measured encounter frequency.

mob_source.authored_source: Custom piece-generation code assigns ordinary block spawners to EntityType.CAVE_SPIDER and EntityType.ZOMBIE_VILLAGER.
mob_source.natural_source: The structure definitions have empty spawn_overrides. Ambient hostile populations depend on effective biome spawning and world conditions; their exact composition is UNKNOWN here.
mob_source.scope: Possible generation paths, not a claim that every mineshaft includes both rooms.

loot_table_source.basis: Direct references in the preserved generation disassemblies. SmallTunnel and BigTunnel include chest-minecart paths.
loot_table_source.effective_injections: UNKNOWN: retained loot-integration and container transformation effects still require attribution.

generated_spawners.basis: The piece code places Blocks.SPAWNER, checks SpawnerBlockEntity, then calls setEntityId.
generated_spawners.limitation: Source-supported capability; room selection, successful placement and active spawning are not established for every generated sample.

authored_or_natural_enemies.authored: Cave-spider and zombie-villager spawner assignments are authored by custom generation code.
authored_or_natural_enemies.natural: No structure-level spawn override is declared; natural spawning remains conditional on the effective biome and world state.
authored_or_natural_enemies.limitation: This does not measure enemy counts or prove a particular live spawn.

underground_surface_classification.value: Underground mining network with a VerticalEntrance generation component
underground_surface_classification.basis: Packaged step is underground_structures. BetterMineshaftStructure selects initial Y from the frozen -55 through 30 range and begins generation with VerticalEntrance.
underground_surface_classification.limitation: Initial Y is not total vertical size. The entrance envelope uses maximum build height and does not prove occupied blocks or a visible surface opening.

groups.name: CTOV Village
groups.rationale: One civilian settlement family with 22 architectural and placement designs, each with small, medium and large variants. All 66 roots share the Lithostitched jigsaw assembly contract, empty spawn overrides and civilian template content. Definition differences are restricted to biome constraints, authored start pool, expansion size and the underground start offset. Fortified, canopy, underground and biome/material designs remain explicit variants rather than separate family counts, consistent with the vanilla and Towns & Towers village grouping. Houses, streets, jobsites and injected taverns remain components. CTOV hostile outposts remain a separate family because their authored ravagers and monster spawn overrides establish a different encounter identity. Missing components and effective-runtime limitations remain unresolved where recorded.

intended_hostility.assessment: Civilian village with authored residents and animals; no authored hostile entity in resolved templates.
intended_hostility.basis: All 66 size/design variants share empty spawn_overrides. Resolved templates include villagers and passive or defensive mobs. Architecture, fortifications, canopy construction and below-surface placement are design variations, not evidence of a different hostile encounter role. Natural spawns, raids and runtime changes can still create danger.

authored_or_natural_enemies.basis: Resolved template entity NBT contains civilian, passive or defensive mobs and possibly display entities. Empty structure spawn_overrides leave natural spawning dependent on biome and world state.
authored_or_natural_enemies.limitation: Potential sources only. Missing components, entity placement settings, processors and runtime transformations can affect generated content. This is not an observed population or a complete account of runtime replacements.

generated_spawners.basis: No spawner blocks or generation markers in the resolved reachable templates.
generated_spawners.limitation: Applies to resolved templates only. Missing components and external generation hooks are not proven spawner-free; no per-start live count is claimed.

underground_surface_classification.value: Surface-projected village family with a below-surface design variant
underground_surface_classification.basis: Every root projects to WORLD_SURFACE_WG; the three underground-design roots use offset -14, the other 63 use zero. All share the surface_structures generation step.
underground_surface_classification.limitation: Start intent only. Preserve underground, canopy and fortified designs separately within the family. Room elevations, terrain exposure and visual discovery are not proved by the generation step or start offset.

groups.name: Integrated Stronghold
groups.rationale: One assembled stronghold rooted at the fountain start pool. Dining halls, libraries, prisons, portal rooms and other connected pools are components of this structure, not independent families. The Integrated Stronghold and Better Strongholds suppression hooks target vanilla StructureType.STRONGHOLD. This root uses integrated_api:generic_structure and the Better Strongholds root uses yungsapi:yung_jigsaw, so neither matches those vanilla-type filters. Their distinct assembled designs remain separate families, while vanilla is retained as a suppressed candidate. This resolves the replacement boundary without claiming observed placement, completed attributes or an effective Eye of Ender target.

mob_source.basis: Packaged structure definition. This is a natural monster-spawn override within piece bounds, not an authored spawn count.
mob_source.authored_content: Reachable template entities, spawners and processors remain to be attributed.

underground_surface_classification.value: Underground start with assembled surface exposure unresolved

custom_generation_settings.position: Chunk world X/Z origin. Y = minY + 15 + nextInt(abs(seaLevel - 20 - (minY + 15))). Reject seaLevel <=30 or height span <10.
custom_generation_settings.processor: DeepslateProcessor replaces stone/mossy cobblestone below Y=0 with deepslate/tuff. Positions, slime/spawner markers and chest NBT are preserved.

intended_hostility.value: Authored slime encounter
intended_hostility.basis: Six slime markers and one slime-spawner marker interpreted by the custom piece, rather than inferred from the family name.

mob_source.direct_creation: Each slime marker requests a slime finalized with STRUCTURE spawn reason and size nextInt(3)+1.
mob_source.spawner_source: One template spawner marker requests a vanilla slime spawner.
mob_source.natural_source: StructureSettings has no spawn overrides. Additional natural spawning depends on biome and world conditions; exact population is not claimed.
mob_source.scope: Marker requests, not guaranteed successful creation, insertion or live mob counts.

loot_table_source.basis: Template chest NBT is preserved by the direct processor; packaged source selection is bound by test_slime_cave_sources.py.
loot_table_source.effective_injections: UNKNOWN: relevant retained global loot/container transformations still require reconciliation.

generated_spawners.placement: The spawner DATA marker places the block and loads slime SpawnData when its block entity exists. Both custom light ranges are inclusive 0..7.
generated_spawners.scope: Source request at one marker, not proof of successful placement or live spawning.

authored_or_natural_enemies.authored: Direct slime creation and the slime spawner are authored by data-marker handling.
authored_or_natural_enemies.natural: Additional natural spawning is conditional on biome and world state; no structure-specific spawn override.

underground_surface_classification.basis: UNDERGROUND_STRUCTURES with BURY terrain adjustment and the captured below-sea-level placement algorithm.
underground_surface_classification.limitation: Not proof of actual surface cover or absence of natural cave exposure in every world.

groups.rationale: One modular Mega Ship family with material, attachment and wreck variants. Every variant has corresponding initial hull, middle and end modules, sharing 48 by 48 by 48 initial/middle bounds and 35 by 20 by 23 end bounds. Side and upper attachments differ. The versioned elements select the original arena_2, arena_3 and arena_4 paths on Minecraft 1.21.1; the packaged 1_21_9 alternatives are not additional live variants here. Its connected trial/vault encounter design is distinct from the pyramid and from the house and tower sites. Membership is based on the complete selected pool graph and packaged contents. Biome names, generic codec and template counts alone are not the grouping rule. These source decisions do not establish actual generation, occupied dimensions or live encounter frequency.

groups.name: Moog's Nether Structures Ruin Fragments

The unnumbered very_small_nether_brick definition still duplicates very_small_blackstone and reaches the same template; both registry IDs remain for placement accounting. Circular encounter ruins preserve an organized encounter-space arrangement and the ruined portal preserves an obsidian frame; those are separate designs from these fragments. The lower components are pieces, not separate families. Preserve the lava variant without loot separately within the family; shared well identity does not imply equal rewards or assembled height. The inspected upper pieces share a compact roofed well-pavilion form; the medium crimson and warped pieces are matching material variants. Their lower shafts remain components. This form differs from the tall framed soul-fire installation and the cultivation building, so those are separate designs. Effective placement remains unresolved.

groups.name: Moog's Nether Structures Circular Ruin

Blackstone has a wither skeleton spawner and houses loot references, while nether brick has piglin and piglin brute spawners and no packaged loot references. These differences remain attributed to their individual templates in the joined inventory. Shared circular ruin identity does not imply equivalent hostility, rewards or occupied geometry. Both layouts retain a circular arrangement of upright ruin elements around an encounter space. This arrangement differs from generic fragments and from the broken obsidian portal frame. The cemetery instead uses an organized rectangular grave plot. These design relationships are resolved; effective generation remains unresolved.

Both inspected templates share the same compact gabled-house form and remain variants. That form differs from the long hall-and-tower large house and the upright framed warped-house design; these house relationships are resolved without relying on size or material labels alone. Effective generation and natural spawning remain unresolved.

processor_effects.pillar_extension: PillarProcessor matches the complete trigger state and extends along the configured direction within build bounds, strict length distance and its land/replaceability checks. It skips extension outside the WorldGenRegion center chunk. The default length ceiling is 1000, direction DOWN and forced_placement false; selected red-glass columns explicitly force length 2. These are source bounds, not observed heights.
processor_effects.pillar_delegation: Extension positions invoke referenced processors through processBlock only. The direct chunk write uses returned state at the extension position and discards returned NBT. It does not invoke delegate finalizeProcessing. Thus the jungle surface archaeology delegate is not applied through this pillar path.
processor_effects.surface_loot: CappedStructureSurfaceProcessor implements finalizeProcessing, requires equal original/processed list sizes, filters to placement bounds and surface eligibility, then invokes its delegate processBlock. It keeps only nonnull changed results in the processed list. The jungle delegate can assign suspicious-gravel archaeology loot on eligible template blocks. Effective engine invocation and placed archaeology blocks remain UNKNOWN.
processor_effects.material_replacements: Noise and random replacement callers operate on the configured input block and preserve position/NBT, delegating compatible state-property copying to GeneralUtils. Their selected monument outputs are material changes, not additional direct entity or loot assignments. Exact patterns are not measured.
processor_effects.nether_lava: Selected rules change air to lava under a 0..31 Y-position predicate. YValuePosRuleTest tests its second position argument inclusively. Effective engine argument mapping and predicate registration remain unverified; no converted-block observation is claimed.
processor_effects.reproducibility: The surface finalizer uses Collections.shuffle(List) without a supplied seeded random. This establishes a source-level ordering limitation, not an observed world mismatch. Full processor seed determinism is not claimed.
processor_effects.remaining: Engine processing/finalization behavior, effective registry activation, relevant retained modifications, land-helper semantics, generated-world attribution and final geometry remain unresolved.

groups.name: IDAS castle
groups.rationale: One castle-settlement family with three equal-weight authored designs in the same start pool, not three interchangeable material skins. Castle1 is a compact battlemented enclosure, castle2 has a denser tower and courtyard arrangement, and castle3 has a large roofed keep and outer walls. Main template extents are respectively 36 by 23 by 26, 41 by 36 by 53 and 106 by 66 by 84. Their corresponding bottom templates are 36 by 6 by 26, 41 by 1 by 53 and 106 by 3 by 84; each main connects to its own bottom through matching idas:bottom names. All designs connect to the same villager and guard entity-component pools. Castle1 and castle2 additionally connect to plains village town centers; castle3 has no such connector. Preserve all three settlement layouts as design alternatives, consistent with the multi-design village grouping, rather than counting foundations, entity templates or the 136 reachable templates (including shared village pieces) as additional castle families. All three main/bottom pairs lack physical spawners, while their loot and authored contents differ: castle1 includes villagers and farm animals with castle, library and vanilla village loot; castle2 includes guards, mounts, displays, seat and glue with castle, library and throne loot; castle3 includes mounts and displays with castle, bedroom, food, library, throne and borrowed witches-treestump loot. Castle2 retains one authored entity lacking an ID. Shared loot does not merge castle with witches treestump. Keep the common castle processor and distinct element terrain kernels, and preserve the selected village-tavern component link. generation.vertical_anchor: WorldGenLevel.getSeaLevel() replaces the incoming origin Y before template placement.
generation.rotation: isZAxis=false uses COUNTERCLOCKWISE_90; true retains default rotation.
generation.processing_stage: StructureTemplate.placeInWorld runs before the custom processor list is applied in order.
generation.selection: Randomly choose from remaining inline placed features; return on first successful place result, otherwise remove that candidate and continue until exhausted.
generation.success_limit: AbstractTemplateFeature discards the placeInWorld boolean. BridgeFeature returns true for a non-null loaded template; this does not prove all blocks were placed.
generation.scope: Captured generation control flow, not observed placement success, discovery frequency or final support geometry. Full processor effects and placement eligibility still require reconciliation.

support_geometry.source: DynamicLegProcessor calls ITemplateFeatureProcessor.generatePillarDown for template support markers.
support_geometry.behavior: Replace the marker with the first supplied block state, then descend at fixed X/Z through air or liquid while Y > 0, using the second supplied state. Stop at Y <= 0 or a block that is neither air nor liquid.
support_geometry.vertical_size: Template Y sizes describe the bridge body only. Supports may extend below that envelope; total occupied height depends on terrain and placement success.
support_geometry.limit: The descent uses literal Y=0, not the dimension minimum build height. setBlock return values are discarded; this is source-derived placement intent, not an observed completed pillar.

placement_eligibility.source: BridgePlacement.getPositions in the captured generator manifest.
placement_eligibility.sampling_plane: Sea level minus one. The generator subsequently anchors the template at sea level.
placement_eligibility.search: For each lateral offset from width/2 + widthOffset + 1 (inclusive) to 16 - width/2 - widthOffset (exclusive), try longitudinal offsets 0 through 15. Integer division is used. Swap X/Z roles for non-Z-axis variants. Return only the first valid candidate, or an empty stream.
placement_eligibility.banks: Endpoint centers are length + 1 blocks apart. Both must canOcclude and have WORLD_SURFACE height <= sea level. At each endpoint, count the center plus contiguous qualifying lateral cells on each side, stopping that side at its first failure or width/2. Each endpoint count must reach numSolidBlocksNeeded.
placement_eligibility.span: Every cell from lateral -width/2 through width/2 and longitudinal minWaterZ through maxWaterZ (inclusive) must satisfy BlockState.liquid at sea level minus one. The predicate does not specifically test water.
placement_eligibility.surface_classification: Surface liquid-crossing placement intent, supported by the bank heightmap and sea-level checks. This is not proof of player visibility or observed generation frequency.
placement_eligibility.scope: These are the custom terrain checks. Biome filtering, selector variants and rarity modifiers remain separate packaged constraints; no world observation is inferred.

biome_and_modifier_constraints.rarity_scope: All 22 inline variants specify chance=3 after their terrain filter. This is not an observed bridge frequency or an independent one-in-three chance per chunk; the selector can try multiple candidates.
biome_and_modifier_constraints.rng_initializer: Consumes two nextLong values, forces their low bits to one, combines them with candidate X/Z and constants to reseed the supplied random source, then returns the same position. No additional position or eligibility test.
biome_and_modifier_constraints.scope: Biome resolution uses existing merged packaged tags and the verified biome registry. Dimension overlap uses the captured live possible-biome lists, not observed successful bridge placement. Standalone configuration registration and external modifications remain unresolved.

initialization.entrypoint: The NeoForge constructor calls the common init method. Common init scans the mod module package with YungAutoRegister.scanPackageForAnnotations, then calls Services.MODULES.loadModules().
initialization.neoforge_module_loader: The packaged NeoForgeModulesLoader delegates directly to IModulesLoader.loadModules. That default method contains only return, so this module-loader implementation performs no configuration registration.
initialization.scope: Verified direct entrypoint and module-loader implementation. Service selection and annotation-driven registration remain separate from this finding. This does not establish absence of all configuration, data-driven or external generation controls.

families.rationale: All 22 configured variants feed one bridge selector and use the same bank-and-liquid-span placement and BridgeFeature. Material, length, intact/broken design and axis orientation vary within the river-crossing bridge family. The selector itself and three packaged templates outside its traced links are not additional families.

yungsextras:feature_entrypoints.mechanism: NeoForge biome modifiers add placed features, which reference configured features. No yungsextras structure-registry roots are present.
yungsextras:feature_entrypoints.relationship: The 62 configured/placed variants are assigned exactly once to ten authored-form families below. Single and double swamp arches are one family despite separate generator types. Template links and variant-specific content remain preserved. This grouping does not close required attributes or broader provider coverage.
yungsextras:feature_entrypoints.removal_scope: The packaged removal targets minecraft:desert_well at surface_structures in the same three resolved desert biomes as desert additions. Their captured dimension overlap is overworld only. Configuration/registration effects and generated-world consequences remain to be reconciled.
yungsextras:feature_entrypoints.scope: Runtime registry and packaged biome-modifier entrypoints, all 62 template links/envelopes, packaged contents and direct generator/processor rules are recorded below. Canonical families, effective retained-stack effects, configuration/provider coverage and remaining required attributes are incomplete. Forge-path duplicates are not additional NeoForge contributions.

biome_constraints.scope: Existing merged packaged tag resolution against registered biomes. Overlap with captured live dimension possible-biome lists is not proof of successful generation or observed removal. Optional absent members are not silently promoted to active biomes.

template_membership.scope: 59 explicit configured location links and three code-bound links cover all 62 packaged templates. JSON-explicit and code-bound paths remain separate. Sizes are unrotated template envelopes, not occupied or processed world geometry. Generated content and family reconciliation remain incomplete.

packaged_template_content.scope: All 62 packaged templates have empty entity lists. Only the four named templates contain block entities: three chests and eight campfires, with no stored spawner block entities. The two chest-bearing templates are linked through verified generator code, separately from the 59 JSON-explicit links. This is packaged content, not observed loot, full generated content or absence of custom spawner/entity/loot effects.

desert_generator_templates.template_call: Each class constructs its static ID with ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath and passes that ID to inherited createTemplateFromCenter.
desert_generator_templates.anchor: ChillzoneDesertFeature and DesertGiantTorchFeature pass the ground anchor above(); DesertSmallRuinsFeature passes the ground anchor itself.
desert_generator_templates.centering: The helper subtracts half the template X/Z dimensions using integer division, leaves Y unchanged, and calls StructureTemplate.placeInWorld with default StructurePlaceSettings.
desert_generator_templates.success_limit: The helper discards the placeInWorld boolean, then runs the processor list and returns the loaded template. Each of these classes returns whether the template is non-null. This is not proof that all template blocks were placed.
desert_generator_templates.scope: FeatureModule class/field AutoRegister annotations bind the yungsextras namespace and feature names to constructor-bound classes. Packaged configured type fields and captured template calls complete the three code-based links. Remaining terrain/content effects are still open; the JSON-explicit mapping remains separate.

desert_well_generation.processor_binding: DesertWellFeature.useProcessors selects only FeatureProcessorModule.DESERT_WELL_PROCESSOR. The module constructs DesertWellProcessor; its register helper returns the same instance. AbstractNbtFeature runs it after template placement.
desert_well_generation.terrain: Descend through empty blocks while Y > 7. Require the landing block default state in BlockTags.SAND. At each depth 1 through 7 below the landing position, reject an empty block at the center or any of the four diagonal corners at the configured radius. These are non-empty checks, not full-volume solid-ground checks.
desert_well_generation.template_anchor: Pass the configured location to createTemplateFromCenter at landing position six blocks down. The unrotated template envelope is centered in X/Z by the inherited helper.
desert_well_generation.brown_marker_rule: Choose cap nextInt(3)+2. In template filter order, select each brown stained glass marker with nextFloat()<0.1 until the cap; replace other markers with sand. If fewer than two were selected, convert previously unselected markers in order until two or until exhausted.
desert_well_generation.yellow_marker_rule: Choose independent budget nextInt(3)+2. In template filter order, select each yellow stained glass marker with nextFloat()<0.4 while budget remains, decrementing on selection; replace others with sand. There is no minimum-fill second pass.
desert_well_generation.loot_assignment: placeSusSand requests SUSPICIOUS_SAND with update flag 3, discards the setBlock result, and assigns the loot table with position.asLong() as seed only if a BRUSHABLE_BLOCK entity is present.
desert_well_generation.extra_loot_contents: One archaeology pool with one roll and diamond, emerald and gold_ingot item entries; no explicit weights or conditions. Packaged contents only, before external loot modification.
desert_well_generation.scope: Source-supported placement and loot creation rules, not observed successful placements or reward counts. The shared template helper does not propagate placeInWorld failure. Family grouping and effective retained-stack loot modifications remain unresolved.

swamp_generation.processor_binding: All six concrete classes inherit AbstractSwampFeature.useProcessors without overriding it. This selects only SWAMP_FEATURE_PROCESSOR, constructed as SwampFeatureProcessor by FeatureProcessorModule. The inherited template helper runs it after placement.
swamp_generation.anchor: All six descend through empty blocks while Y > 2 and pass the resulting position directly to createTemplateFromCenter with the configured location. The helper centers X/Z by integer half-size, leaves Y unchanged and uses default StructurePlaceSettings.
swamp_generation.terrain_checks: Reject if any listed XYZ offset from the landing position is empty. These are selected-point non-empty checks, not full-footprint solidity checks, and contain no biome/block-tag test in these six classes.
swamp_generation.support_columns: Each gray stained glass marker is replaced with a stone-brick selector result. Starting one block below it, continue downward replacing air, liquid or replaceable blocks until encountering a state satisfying none of those predicates. This loop has no explicit minimum-Y guard and discards setBlock results. Support depth is terrain-dependent and is not bounded by the packaged template height.
swamp_generation.masonry: Gray stained glass and existing stone bricks use STONE_BRICK_SELECTOR, initialized with stone bricks and mossy/cracked stone-brick additions. Light-gray stained glass uses STONE_BRICK_STAIRS_SELECTOR with a random horizontal facing. Existing stone-brick stairs use that selector while preserving facing, half, shape and waterlogged properties. The stair selector is initialized with stone-brick stairs and a mossy-stair addition.
swamp_generation.candles: Green candles are replaced with a uniformly indexed choice from candle, white, gray, light_gray, brown, green, purple and black candles. Count is nextInt(4)+1 and LIT is nextFloat()<0.1. The processor writes the selected default state with those two properties, using update flag 2.
swamp_generation.scope: Direct source-derived placement and appearance effects for six generator types, not six accepted families or observed visibility. Template contents are recorded separately. Selector-library implementation, external retained-stack effects, natural mobs and full generated-world outcomes are not established by these classes. Generator success still means a non-null template, not verified complete placement.

desert_surface_generation.landing: All four descend through empty blocks while Y > 2. Each requires the landing block default state to match BlockTags.SAND and four selected positions at landing Y to satisfy BlockState.isSolid(). This is not a full-footprint ground check.
desert_surface_generation.placement: Chillzone, giant torch and obelisk center their template one block above landing. Small ruins center at landing Y. Obelisk reads the configured location; the other three fixed template links are recorded separately.
desert_surface_generation.processors: All four directly inherit AbstractNbtFeature and do not override useProcessors. The base initializes processors from useProcessors(), which returns a new empty ArrayList. These classes therefore add no custom post-placement processor through this path.
desert_surface_generation.scope: Source-derived terrain and placement rules only. Packaged chest and campfire contents remain recorded separately. This does not prove successful placement, full retained-stack content effects or observed visual discoverability.

initialization.entrypoint: The NeoForge constructor calls the common init method. Common init scans the mod module package with YungAutoRegister.scanPackageForAnnotations, then calls Services.MODULES.loadModules().
initialization.neoforge_module_loader: The packaged NeoForgeModulesLoader delegates directly to IModulesLoader.loadModules. That default method contains only return, so this module-loader implementation performs no configuration registration.
initialization.scope: Verified direct entrypoint and module-loader implementation. Service selection and annotation-driven registration remain separate from this finding. This does not establish absence of all configuration, data-driven or external generation controls.

betterendisland:platform_gateway.mechanism: Conditional mixin replacements of vanilla EndPlatformFeature.createEndPlatform and EndGatewayFeature.place, not additional structure-registry roots.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.hooks: Both inject at HEAD and are cancellable. With useVanillaSpawnPlatform false, the platform hook invokes the custom generator, discards its boolean and cancels vanilla execution. With useVanillaEndGateways false, the gateway hook returns the custom generator boolean. True leaves the respective vanilla path alone.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.packaged_template_content: Both linked templates have empty entities and block_entities. This excludes neither processor-created blocks nor the gateway block explicitly placed by code.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.platform_placement: Offset the input position down 14 blocks, then subtract integer half template X/Z. Use Rotation.NONE, pivot (3,0,3), IGNORE_WATERLOGGING and placement flag 2. A fresh RandomSource.create() is used rather than a supplied seeded source. The destroyBlocks boolean is forwarded to placeTemplate but not read there.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.gateway_placement: Subtract integer half template X/Y/Z from context origin. Use context random, Rotation.NONE, pivot (1,0,1), IGNORE_WATERLOGGING and placement flag 2. After the template call, request END_GATEWAY at context origin with flag 3, regardless of the template helper result. If configuration has an exit and the block entity is an EndGateway, set its exit position/exactness and mark changed.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.processors: Platform static processor list is empty; gateway static list contains DragonEggProcessor. Both then add ObsidianProcessor with dragon-kill count, read only when the supplied accessor is a ServerLevel with a non-null dragon fight, otherwise zero. Direct effects are recorded below.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.success_limits: Missing templates log a warning and return false. Loaded-template helpers discard placeInWorld boolean and return true. Platform hook cancellation does not depend on success. Gateway returns its template helper result, not whether portal-block placement or exit initialization succeeded.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.scope: Source, packaged template and registry-r1 runtime activation attribution. Family reconciliation, dimension applicability and generated-world observations remain open.

processor_effects.DragonEggProcessor: Reads the existing world block at the incoming target position. If it is DRAGON_EGG, replaces the incoming block state with default DRAGON_EGG while preserving position and incoming NBT. Otherwise returns the incoming block unchanged. This preserves an existing egg, rather than creating an egg reward at an empty target.
processor_effects.ObsidianProcessor: Only incoming OBSIDIAN is transformed. Obtain random from StructurePlaceSettings.getRandom(target position); clamp dragon kills to 0..10; use lerp(clampedKills/10.0, 0, 0.5) as the nextFloat threshold for CRYING_OBSIDIAN, otherwise default OBSIDIAN. Preserve position and incoming NBT. Non-obsidian input passes through unchanged.
processor_effects.scope: Direct block substitution only. Neither processor directly spawns entities, configures spawners or assigns loot tables. This does not establish engine/API behavior, ordinary block drops, external retained-stack modifications or observed world results.

configuration.binding: BEIConfigNeoForge defines these keys and defaults. ConfigModuleNeoForge.init registers the spec as COMMON under this filename. bakeConfig copies each ConfigValue into the corresponding BetterEndIslandCommon.CONFIG field. ConfigModule constructor defaults match the frozen values.
configuration.platform_gateway_effect: Both vanilla-generation toggles are false, selecting the custom branch in their captured hooks when those hooks apply.
configuration.scope: Verified frozen values and direct key-to-field assignment. This does not prove entrypoint invocation, effective mixin activation or successful world generation. Tower/egg/bell consumers require separate attribution.

mixin_declaration.scope: NeoForge mod metadata declares this required common mixin configuration, which lists both captured hooks and has no plugin entry. This establishes packaged application intent, not direct runtime transformation or world-generation observation.

spike_podium_generators.spike_hook: SpikeFeatureMixin replaces getSpikesForLevel with the custom result. Its cancellable HEAD placeSpike hook calls BetterSpikeFeature with an accessor-is-WorldGenRegion flag, then cancels vanilla. Neither hook has a local configuration condition.
spike_podium_generators.spike_variants: SpikeCacheLoader shuffles 0..9 and creates ten spikes with height 76 + 3*j. chooseTemplates maps (height - 73)/3 to 1..10, then remaps 10 to 9: indices 1..8 once and 9 twice per generated list. Templates are betterendisland:pillar_{initial|guarded|broken}_{index} and betterendisland:pillar_bottom_{index}. WorldGenRegion selects initial; otherwise random nextFloat below 0.2 selects guarded, else broken. The loader guarded flag (j equals 1 or 2) is not consulted by chooseTemplates. This describes the captured loader path, not arbitrary externally supplied EndSpike objects.
spike_podium_generators.spike_geometry: Top anchor is (spike center X, 70 when BetterEndIslandCommon.betterEnd is true, otherwise 60, spike center Z); bottom anchor is 67 blocks below. Both subtract integer half template X/Z and use the same random rotation with pivot (9,0,9). Each top template envelope is 19x69x19 and each bottom is 19x67x19. Adjacent vertical anchors give a combined 19x136x19 nominal envelope per spike, including air, not occupied-block height. The runtime/source derivation below selects betterEnd=true, top Y=70; this is not an occupied-world measurement.
spike_podium_generators.spike_entity_source: After both template helpers return true, and only when the WorldGenRegion flag is false, request an END_CRYSTAL at (center X + 0.5, anchor Y + IEndSpike crystal offset, center Z + 0.5). Beam target and invulnerability come from SpikeConfiguration. Request BEDROCK one block below. Entity-add and block-write booleans are discarded. EndSpikeMixin supplies the recorded crystal offsets; this is a direct entity request, not a spawner or observed successful spawn.
spike_podium_generators.podium_variants: Constructor arguments are isInitialSpawn, isBottomOnly, isActive, in that order. Bottom-only selects betterendisland:tower_bottom_open; otherwise initial selects betterendisland:tower_initial and false selects betterendisland:tower_broken. The invocation mapping and frozen tower switches are resolved below; successful runtime placement is not inferred.
spike_podium_generators.podium_geometry: Use context origin and random, subtract integer half template X/Z, Rotation.NONE, and pivot (3,0,3) for bottom-only or (14,0,14) otherwise. Full tower envelope is 29x27x29; bottom-only is 7x11x7. These include air and are not occupied-block measurements.
spike_podium_generators.podium_entity_source: When isInitialSpawn is true, after the template helper, request four EndCrystal entities, one eight blocks in each horizontal cardinal direction from origin.above(6), with X/Z centered by +0.5. Set showBottom false and invulnerable true. This branch does not check template-helper success and discards entity-add results. It establishes direct authored entity requests, not successful observed generation or hostile-mob spawning.
spike_podium_generators.processors: Spike static order: three BlockReplaceProcessor instances (orange terracotta selector with obsidian/crying obsidian; magenta terracotta selector with air/crying obsidian/obsidian; purple concrete selector with obsidian), then DragonEggProcessor, then per-placement ObsidianProcessor. Podium: gray concrete/bedrock BlockReplaceProcessor, DragonEggProcessor, active red concrete/end portal or inactive red concrete/air BlockReplaceProcessor, then ObsidianProcessor. For these instances all four optional flags are false. BlockReplaceProcessor matches incoming block type, selects output with settings random at target position, preserves incoming position/NBT and passes nonmatching input unchanged. No optional property copying, facing/half randomization or waterlog preservation applies. Configured outputs exclude water/lava, so its fluid-tick branch does not apply. Selector arguments are not asserted as observed frequencies.
spike_podium_generators.success_limits: Both template helpers warn and return false when the template is absent; otherwise they discard StructureTemplate.placeInWorld boolean and return true. Both use IGNORE_WATERLOGGING and flag 2. A false spike helper logs an error and returns before subsequent steps. Podium returns its helper boolean even though initial crystal requests can occur after helper failure.
spike_podium_generators.scope: Partial attribution from the preserved full generators. Does not establish final families, complete generated contents, absence of loot/spawners, runtime activation or world observations. Resolve only dependencies needed for those Item 8 attributes.
spike_podium_generators.spike_layout: SpikeCacheLoader places ten centers around radius 42 when betterEnd is true, otherwise 54, using floor(radius*cos(angle)) and floor(radius*sin(angle)), angle 2*(-pi + pi*i/10), i=0..9. BetterEndIslandCommon.init assigns betterEnd from Services.PLATFORM.isModLoaded("betterend"). The runtime/source derivation below selects the true branch (radius 42).
spike_podium_generators.template_content_scope: These 39 spike/podium templates plus the two previously linked platform/gateway templates account for every template in this provider catalog. All have empty stored entities; only the two full tower templates have block entities (one bell each). This does not erase the direct code-created crystal source or establish complete runtime provider coverage.

podium_invocation.configuration: ExitPortalUtils.spawnPortal selects spawnCentralTowerOnResummon when hasDragonEverSpawned is true, otherwise spawnCentralTowerInitially. Both frozen values are true, selecting BetterEndPodiumFeature in either state when the bound configuration applies. The vanilla branch is consequently not selected by these frozen values.
podium_invocation.arguments: The helper arguments after fight/level are isActive, isBottomOnly and a vanilla-branch crystal-suppression flag. The two-boolean overload supplies false for the last flag. The custom constructor receives (fight.isFirstExitPortalSpawn(), isBottomOnly, isActive), and placement uses portalLocation.below(5), FeatureConfiguration.NONE, level chunk generator and a fresh RandomSource.create(). Placement boolean is discarded.
podium_invocation.initial_scan: EndDragonFightMixin.scanForInitialState calls spawnPortal(false,false) when no active exit portal exists and findExitPortal is null. This requests a full inactive tower; first-exit flag determines initial versus broken template. The mixin constructor initializes that flag true; persisted/restored state applicability remains separate.
podium_invocation.missing_portal_recovery: EndDragonFightMixin.spawnDragon calls spawnPortal(false,false) then spawnPortal(true,true) if portalLocation is null and findExitPortal returns null. This requests a full inactive tower followed by an active bottom-only portal. The first helper clears the first-exit flag before the second call.
podium_invocation.dragon_death: For the tracked dragon UUID, setDragonKilled always calls spawnPortal(true,true). Its preceding full-tower call requires zero prior kills, spawnCentralTowerInitially false and spawnCentralTowerOnResummon true, so that preceding branch is disabled by the frozen true/true tower settings.
podium_invocation.reset: The reset method sets first-exit false, then directly constructs BetterEndPodiumFeature(true,false,false) when spawnCentralTowerInitially is true. It places at portalLocation.below(5) with a fresh random source and discards the result. The direct constructor flag therefore selects an initial full tower regardless of the reset first-exit field.
podium_invocation.origin_adjustment: ExitPortalUtils retains a non-null portalLocation with Y >= 5. Otherwise it requests WorldgenUtils.getSurfacePosAt(level,0,0), descends while the block is bedrock and Y exceeds sea level, and falls back to (0,65,0) if Y remains below 5. It updates portalLocation before placement. WorldgenUtils.getSurfacePosAt scans downward from getMaxBuildHeight while Y > getMinBuildHeight and returns the first END_STONE block Y, not the highest arbitrary solid block. It returns -1 if no match, causing the recorded Y=65 fallback.
podium_invocation.success_limits: spawnPortal returns void and sets first-exit false after the placement branch, even if the custom feature returned false. A call proves neither template placement nor successful entity insertion. Exceptions can prevent reaching the final flag update.
podium_invocation.scope: Direct source and frozen-value derivation for the captured callers, including respawn calls below. Effective runtime execution and generated-world observations remain to be reconciled. This does not add a family or imply complete provider coverage.

respawn_generation.stage_binding: DragonRespawnStage static initialization binds class $3 to SUMMONING_PILLARS and class $5 to END. These are phases of one dragon-fight generation path, not separate structure families.
respawn_generation.pillar_rebuild: SUMMONING_PILLARS processes the spike indexed by integer tick/40 when tick modulo 40 is 0 or 39. At 0 it redirects supplied crystal beams; at 39 it requests an explosion and block clearing, then Feature.END_SPIKE.place with SpikeConfiguration(true, singleton spike, beam target (0,128,0)), level chunk generator, fresh random and origin (centerX,45,centerZ). It discards placement success. The captured SpikeFeatureMixin routes this ServerLevel call through the non-WorldGenRegion branch, selecting guarded/broken templates and requesting a crystal.
respawn_generation.pillar_clearance: The rebuild requests a strength-5 BLOCK-interaction explosion at spike center plus 0.5 X/Z and base Y plus crystal offset minus 1. It then removes non-END_STONE blocks in the inclusive X/Z center +/-11 and Y EndSpike.height +/-40 when betterEnd, otherwise +/-30 box. This affects existing blocks; it is not an additional authored family or an observed destruction measurement.
respawn_generation.dragon_source: END.onStart clears the custom stage, sets dragonKilled false and invokes EndDragonFightAccessor.invokeCreateNewDragon. This is a direct authored dragon creation request associated with the arena, separate from stored template entities or a spawner. Successful entity creation remains a runtime claim.
respawn_generation.podium_rebuild: END.onStart calls spawnPortal(false,false,true), requesting a full inactive podium. If hasDragonEverSpawned was already true, it subsequently calls spawnPortal(false,true,true), requesting an inactive bottom-only podium. Both frozen tower flags are true; the last helper argument only suppresses crystals in its unselected vanilla branch. The first-exit flag still determines initial/broken full template. At the end, setHasDragonEverSpawned(true).
respawn_generation.other_material_changes: END.onStart also conditionally replaces existing OBSIDIAN with CRYING_OBSIDIAN using threshold lerp(clamp(dragon kills,0,10)/10,0,0.5). It covers gateway positions for indices 0..19 absent from the remaining-gateways list and a fixed box around END_SPAWN_POINT. These are changes to existing blocks, not new gateway or platform family creation. Block-update results are discarded.
respawn_generation.scope: Recorded source-level generation effects of SUMMONING_PILLARS and END. No new family, observed frequency, successful respawn or completed runtime coverage is asserted. Other phases and external interactions are not exhaustively characterized by this record.

initialization.entrypoint: BetterEndIslandNeoForge constructor sets loadingContextEventBus, calls BetterEndIslandCommon.init, then ConfigModuleNeoForge.init with its ModContainer. This connects the captured common detection and configuration registration paths; it is not direct proof of runtime execution.
initialization.service_selection: Services static initialization loads IPlatformHelper and IModulesLoader using ServiceLoader.load(...).findFirst().orElseThrow(...). The packaged service declarations name NeoForgePlatformHelper and NeoForgeModulesLoader respectively. NeoForgePlatformHelper.isModLoaded delegates to ModList.get().isLoaded(id). NeoForgeModulesLoader delegates to the IModulesLoader default method; no behavior is inferred here for that unexamined default.
initialization.configuration_connection: The constructor config-init call registers the already captured frozen COMMON configuration specification. Common.init assigns betterEnd from the platform helper using mod ID betterend. The preserved runtime loading/configuration evidence and derived betterEnd=true branch are linked below.
initialization.scope: Packaged service declarations and direct call paths only. No new runtime observation or global service-provider uniqueness claim.

runtime_activation.finding: The preserved runtime log records both mods in the mod list and creates their containers, records the two actual NeoForge service selections, applies the six directly relevant mixins and loads the Better End Island configuration. The captured configuration bytes match the frozen file exactly. This resolves runtime mixin/service activation and configuration-file identity for registry-r1.
runtime_activation.better_end_derivation: Combining the recorded betterend mod/container and selected NeoForgePlatformHelper with the captured Common.init assignment and ModList.isLoaded delegation gives betterEnd=true for this stack initialization. Therefore the recorded spike top-anchor branch is Y=70 and loader radius is 42. This is a derivation from runtime loading plus preserved code, not a direct field dump or measured occupied-world extent.
runtime_activation.limitations: Log application records do not prove each generation hook executed or placed a template successfully. No arena, gateway, platform or respawn observation is inferred from readiness or class transformation. Generated-world reconciliation remains open.

generated_world_observations.scope: Accepted Item 7 ordinary seed 42 run-a, minecraft:the_end, block X/Z -64 through 63. Offline extraction of manifest-verified saved regions; no new generation or survey.
generated_world_observations.observation: Saved sections contain obsidian, End Stone bricks, End Stone brick walls and End Stone brick slabs. The selected chunk records contain no block entities. These are actual decoded block-state counts, not unused palette names.
generated_world_observations.attribution: Material presence is consistent with the linked spike templates, but this projection does not preserve individual block positions or establish exclusive provider ownership. Exact template/variant attribution remains UNKNOWN. No podium, gateway or spawn-platform generation is claimed from these counts.
generated_world_observations.limitations: The selection does not cover the whole End. It does not observe ordinary entities, dragon-fight state, respawn events or every reachable generator. Absence of block entities here is not proof that a provider cannot place them elsewhere or on another lifecycle event.

spiral_spire_geometry.preflight: makeSpike chooses H=50+nextInt(20), so H is 50..69, and taper parameter a=5+nextDouble(). It checks the central column from originY-5 through originY+H-1, accepting only air, End Stone, crying obsidian, obsidian or the module myalite_crystal block. Any other central-column block returns before construction. This is not a clearance check of the entire footprint.
spiral_spire_geometry.body: For y=-5 through H-1, skip a negative layer when its central block cannot occlude. Otherwise r=ceil(abs((pi/2-atan((max(0,y)+0.5)/(H/a)))*4)). Iterate X/Z offsets -r+1 through r-1, retaining offsets with x*x+z*z<=r*r. At the square-edge offsets, nextFloat()<0.2 selects NewStoneTypesModule.myaliteBlock; all other body positions use dusky_myalite. Writes use flag 2 and discard success.
spiral_spire_geometry.crystal_spiral: Choose N=(80+nextInt(30))*10, angle magnitude 0.12+nextDouble()*0.16 with random sign, radial growth 0.12+nextDouble()*0.04, and vertical growth nextDouble()*0.2. For i=0..N-1, X/Z are Java-truncated sin/cos(i*angle/10)*i*radialGrowth/10; Y is H+round(i*verticalGrowth/10). Request myalite_crystal at those offsets. Placement probability is one until a chosen cutoff in [0.5*N,0.8*N), then decreases linearly. Repeated rounded positions and discarded write results prevent treating iteration count as occupied blocks.
spiral_spire_geometry.conservative_envelope: Body r<=7, hence body X/Z offsets are within -6..6. Since i<=1089 and radialGrowth<0.16, crystal X/Z integer offsets are within -17..17. Crystal Y<=69+round(1089*0.2/10)=91; body Y>=-5. Thus all requested makeSpike writes fit a conservative 35x97x35 XYZ box relative to the anchor, including empty space. This is an analytic upper envelope, not a typical footprint, an attained maximum or a measured world extent.
spiral_spire_geometry.content: The captured generator directly writes Myalite-related blocks. It does not load templates, assign loot tables, configure physical spawners or request entities. Block behavior, later interactions, ordinary drops and other providers remain separate.
spiral_spire_geometry.classification_scope: One working geological-landmark family is retained as quark:spiral_spire. Procedural construction rather than a template does not exclude a recognizable landmark design. Random height, taper, crystal winding and repeated spires remain variants or instances. This is an Item 8 identity decision, not an Item 9 tier.

zeta_resolution.biome_predicate: CompoundBiomeConfig rejects null and requires both component predicates. BiomeTagConfig passes a non-null holder when any tag matches XOR isBlacklist, so an empty blacklist passes. StrictBiomeConfig compares a registered key location string with biomeStrings XOR isBlacklist; its direct-Biome lambda returns false. SpiralSpiresModule defaults therefore admit minecraft:end_highlands only. Frozen configuration records the same empty tag blacklist and named-biome allowlist. Spiral Spires field binding is resolved in spire_configuration_binding.

quark:stone_generation.mechanism: BigStoneClustersModule and VanillaStoneClustersModule register BigStoneClusterGenerator at UNDERGROUND_DECORATION. NewStoneTypesModule additionally registers OreGenerator at UNDERGROUND_ORES.

dispositions.rationale: The shared cluster context writes one stone state at qualifying positions. Calcite, limestone, jasper, shale and myalite are material variants. The air-placement branch creates terrain rather than an authored room or encounter.
Granite, diorite and andesite use the same cluster writer. These are terrain material contributions; registration alone does not establish that the experimental module is enabled.

The additional ore path writes only the supplied stone default state where its matcher accepts existing terrain. Neither the inspected cluster writer nor the ore writer authors rooms, entities, spawners or container loot.

dispositions.rationale: Individual supported lights and small pedestal/light fixtures, including overgrown variants. There is no independent composed site beyond the fixture; a ruin filename does not create a family.

betterend:biome_ruins.relationship: Ten ruin design families account for thirty templates; five fixture templates contribute no family. Cross-biome material swaps, differing survival/damage, orientations and furnishings remain explicit template variants. These are interpretive architectural groupings, not claims that every variant is a transformed copy or that an original intact building can be reconstructed.
betterend:biome_ruins.scope: Membership of this selected template set is resolved. Cube diagrams assist layout comparison but do not model partial block geometry or establish generated-world placement. Per-template contents and dimensions are retained for required attribute work; no loot, hostility or measured-footprint acceptance is implied.

aether:holiday_tree.mechanism: HolidayTreeDecorator scatters snow or provider-selected presents around suitable base-log positions of the configured tree.

dispositions.rationale: The resulting form is a tree with scattered ground decoration, not an independent building or composed encounter site. The exclusion follows the complete writer and supplied states, not the minecraft:tree codec alone.

aether:holiday_tree.scope: Frozen settings allow seasonal generation in December and January according to the JVM calendar, subject to other placement conditions. Present reward behavior remains relevant content; exclusion does not imply disabled generation, absent rewards or observed placement.

deep_aether:fallen_tree.mechanism: FallenTreeFeature writes horizontal roseroot or rotten-roseroot logs with optional supplied lightcap-mushroom decoration.

dispositions.rationale: Both configurations represent fallen vegetation. Length, orientation, decay and mushrooms do not introduce an independent constructed site or additional family.

deep_aether:fallen_tree.scope: Both packaged configurations and their three Aerglow biome consumers remain attributable. Configured length bounds are inputs, not observed dimensions or guaranteed placement.

regions_unexplored:fallen_tree.mechanism: RUFallenTreeFeature places a stump, then conditionally places a horizontal log run and its attached decoration using six supplied configurations.

dispositions.rationale: The six material and length variants depict fallen vegetation, without an independent constructed site. Stump, log, decorations and each placement selector are not separate families.

regions_unexplored:fallen_tree.scope: The generator can return success after placing only a stump when the full fallen log cannot fit. Retain this limitation and all eight placed variants. Ashen remains a vanilla trial-chamber component, not an additional family.

supplementaries:cave_urn_cache.mechanism: The cave_urns biome modifier adds a freestanding underground placement of urns_patch. The vanilla random patch places simple urn blocks marked treasure=true on supported air positions.

dispositions.rationale: A freestanding group of authored treasure vessels is one cache design. It is generated independently of a building or vegetation feature. Scattered positions and the number of successful urn placements are variants, not additional families.
The galleon pool reuses urns_patch inside the existing ship family. Count the standalone cave cache once, not another family for each urn or for this component reuse.

supplementaries:cave_urn_cache.scope: Membership only. The treasure block state is an authored input, not proof of actual loot contents, successful placement or observed cache occurrence. Effective biome eligibility, disabled-content conditions, urn reward behavior and required attributes remain open. Nine patch tries and six placement repetitions are configured attempts, not observed counts.

underground_surface_classification.basis: Uniform origin heights 16 through 96 above world bottom, followed by moonlight:below_heightmaps with MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES and OCEAN_FLOOR_WG and below_sea_level true. Nine patch tries and six repetitions are attempts, not observed cache counts.

visual_discoverability.source_form: Scattered treasure-state urns on supported air positions below terrain.
visual_discoverability.basis: Packaged feature and placement definitions; concealment and visibility distance are not measured.
